Market today: The market's feeling a bit lighter today. Falling oil prices and easing Middle East tensions are cooling things down, which is helping Treasury yields drop. Lower yields are generally good news for your tech and chip names, as it makes their future earnings look more attractive.

Your holdings: SOXL (-54.92%) and SPAL (-60.95%) are in deep trouble. Both are leveraged ETFs, meaning they decay over time and amplify losses, which is extra painful on margin. Your default stops for these are way too high to be useful. QQQI (-5.97%), QQQ (-3.73%), and SMH (-15.06%) are all very close to their stops and need close monitoring.

Watch: Keep a close eye on Treasury yields; continued drops would be a tailwind. Also, watch for any shifts in the Middle East de-escalation narrative.

Bottom line: Your leveraged positions are a major concern; focus on risk management and respecting your stops on all positions.
plays: Review SOXL and SPAL: Your current stops are ineffective. Consider setting new, tighter stops to protect capital given their leveraged nature and deep losses.
Monitor QQQI, QQQ, and SMH closely: They are all near their stops. Be ready to act if those levels are breached.
No new buys today - hold and watch. There are no compelling catalysts from the headlines to justify initiating new positions right now.
